assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins turned a vague biological question into a quantitative physical one: tunneling-pathway and distance-dependence measurements on ruthenium-modified proteins, and the later hopping picture, underpin how respiratory and photosynthetic enzymes move charge. It states biological chemistry in physical terms with time-resolved kinetics, which is the standard I weigh most heavily.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the clear experimental core of the protein-modification and kinetics program. Marcus theory and Hopfield/Beratan-Onuchic tunneling-pathway theory were foundational and recognized earlier or sit outside this credited pair, so the configuration is neat but the theory share needs care.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation across many proteins and independent groups; the interpretation is stable and widely taught, so recognition would not be premature.
uncertainties: Part of the conceptual foundation (Marcus theory) is already recognized, so the new-discovery boundary must be argued carefully.
Whether the committee would see this as a distinct discovery or an extension of earlier electron-transfer prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a central mechanism in respiration, photosynthesis and water oxidation, and the theory of concerted proton-electron motion together with molecular and electrocatalytic demonstrations gives a physical framework for how energy-converting enzymes work. This is close to the mechanistic questions I consider fundamental in biological energy conversion.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over several groups: Mayer on concerted PCET and bond-weakening thermodynamics, Hammes-Schiffer on the theory, Nocera on biomimetic and solar-fuel systems, Meyer on early electrocatalysis. Three can be chosen but exclude real contributors, and it is a line of work rather than one sharply attributable discovery.
assessment.maturity: Experimental and theoretical confirmation is broad and independent, and the concept is standard in the literature. Timing is plausible, though the practical impact in catalysis is still developing.
uncertainties: Attribution among four leading figures is not cleanly separable.
Possible weight given to the artificial-photosynthesis application rather than the mechanism itself.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's chemistry-driven approach to covalently targeting the KRAS G12C switch-II pocket, and earlier analog-sensitive kinase chemical genetics, opened a target class long regarded as undruggable and produced approved drugs. The discovery rests on well-defined structure-based chemistry and has an unusually clear route from molecular insight to clinical effect.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is unusually clean around one laureate, with the discovery of the cryptic pocket and tethering-based covalent ligands clearly credited to his laboratory. Clinical development by industry built on this but does not displace the originating discovery.
assessment.maturity: Independent structural, biochemical and clinical confirmation now exists, with approved KRAS G12C inhibitors, so maturity is good, though long-term durability of response is still being studied.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as chemistry or as medicine.
Resistance to inhibitors may limit the long-term clinical narrative, though not the chemical discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic-code expansion with orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs lets proteins carry designed chemistry in living cells, a general and original method now used for mechanistic probes, photocrosslinking and spectroscopic labels. Its value to enzymologists in particular is considerable.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first unnatural-amino-acid incorporation in vivo; Chin extended it to multicellular organisms and to quadruplet and ribosome-orthogonal systems. Mehl and Yokoyama also contributed substantially, so three names leave some fair claims out.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced across labs for two decades, though many applications are still tool-like and the systems remain somewhat inefficient for some residues.
uncertainties: Priority among Schultz, Wang and others is a real allocation question.
Impact is mostly methodological, which may be weighed against more mechanistic discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural and mechanistic work on nitrogenase explains how a complex metal cofactor reduces dinitrogen, including the identification of the interstitial carbide in FeMo-cofactor and recent cryo-EM snapshots of turnover states. It is a fundamental problem in biological chemistry, with a long record and strong structural evidence.
assessment.attribution: Rees solved the first structures; Einsle resolved the central light atom; Dean and Seefeldt (with Ribbe) contributed genetics, biochemistry and mechanism. Many strong contributors are credited, and a three-person prize would leave some out, which is a difficult allocation.
assessment.maturity: Structures are replicated and refined over three decades, but the full catalytic mechanism, including how N2 binds and the role of hydride and E4 states, is not settled, so maturity is partial.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 binding and reduction is still debated.
Credit is spread over several long-running groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry lets intact, noncovalent protein complexes, including membrane protein assemblies and their lipid interactions, be weighed and their stoichiometry and subunit composition determined. It is an original, widely adopted analytical method that has changed how complexes are characterized.
assessment.attribution: Robinson, Heck and Chait each made distinct contributions: Robinson on membrane complexes and ion-mobility, Heck on large assemblies and instrumentation, Chait on early complexes and a broad portfolio. Loo and Gross also have claims, so the choice is subjective.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced worldwide and increasingly routine, with commercial instruments; the field is mature. Because mass spectrometry was recognized in 2002, the committee may ask whether this is incremental.
uncertainties: Priority claims among several early groups are not fully separable.
Possible view that it extends an already recognized technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation using PROTACs and molecular glues reprograms the ubiquitin-proteasome machinery by chemical design, creating a new therapeutic modality with a clear chemical principle (induced proximity) and rapidly growing impact.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the first PROTAC concept; Ciulli contributed structure-guided design and VHL ligands. Molecular glue discoveries (Handa, Ito, Sakamoto and others) are a separate thread, making this a compound discovery that may need different recognition.
assessment.maturity: Clinical trials are advancing but no PROTAC has yet become an approved drug; reproducibility is strong in cells, yet long-term clinical validation is lacking, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Compound discovery: PROTACs and molecular glues with different attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers permits room-temperature structures of microcrystals before radiation damage and time-resolved structural movies of reactions, bringing structure and kinetics together, which is attractive for dynamic mechanisms such as photosystem II and photoreceptors.
assessment.attribution: Chapman, Fromme and Schlichting appear as plausible credited names, with Hajdu as a conceptual contributor; the 2011 proof of principle involved a large team, so isolating three people is difficult and the facility builders are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Mechanistic payoff from time-resolved experiments is still developing and some interpretations of intermediates have been debated; the method is validated, but the scientific harvest is not yet complete.
uncertainties: Large team effort makes attribution difficult.
Time-resolved results are still being scrutinized.
